passages.text: This is the burden of the word of the LORD to Israel through Malachi: “I have loved you,” says the LORD. But you ask, “How have You loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” declares the LORD. “Yet Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated, and I have made his mountains a wasteland and left his inheritance to the desert jackals.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave a message to Israel through Malachi.
The LORD spoke to Israel.
The LORD said, “I have loved you.”
Israel asked, “How have You loved us?”
The LORD answered.
The LORD said, “Esau was Jacob’s brother.”
The LORD said, “I loved Jacob.”
The LORD said, “I hated Esau.”
The LORD made Esau’s mountains a wasteland.
The LORD left Esau’s inheritance to desert jackals.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֥א דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּיַ֖ד מַלְאָכִֽי׃ אָהַ֤בְתִּי אֶתְכֶם֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמָּ֣ה אֲהַבְתָּ֑נוּ הֲלוֹא־ אָ֨ח עֵשָׂ֤ו לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וָאֹהַ֖ב אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹֽב׃ וְאֶת־ עֵשָׂ֖ו שָׂנֵ֑אתִי וָאָשִׂ֤ים אֶת־ הָרָיו֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְאֶת־ נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְתַנּ֥וֹת מִדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: Though Edom may say, “We have been devastated, but we will rebuild the ruins,” this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “They may build, but I will demolish. They will be called the Land of Wickedness, and a people with whom the LORD is indignant forever.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to Edom.
Edom says, “We have been devastated.”
Edom says, “We will rebuild the ruins.”
The LORD of Hosts says, “They may build.”
I will demolish what they build.
People will call their land the Land of Wickedness.
People will call them a people with whom the LORD is angry forever.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֹאמַ֨ר אֱד֜וֹם רֻשַּׁ֗שְׁנוּ וְנָשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנֶ֣ה חֳרָב֔וֹת כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הֵ֥מָּה יִבְנ֖וּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶהֱר֑וֹס וְקָרְא֤וּ לָהֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל רִשְׁעָ֔ה וְהָעָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־ זָעַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: You will see this with your own eyes, and you yourselves will say, ‘The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.’ ”
passages.sermon:
You are the people of Israel.
You will see these things with your own eyes.
You will say, “The LORD is great.”
The LORD is great even beyond the borders of Israel.
passages.original: וְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם תִּרְאֶ֑ינָה וְאַתֶּ֤ם תֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל לִגְב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. But if I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is your fear of Me?” says the LORD of Hosts to you priests who despise My name. “But you ask, ‘How have we despised Your name?’
passages.sermon:
A son honors his father.
A servant honors his master.
I am the LORD of Hosts.
I speak to you priests.
You despise My name.
If I am a father, where is My honor?
If I am a master, where is your fear of Me?
You ask Me, “How have we despised Your name?”
passages.original: בֵּ֛ן יְכַבֵּ֥ד אָ֖ב וְעֶ֣בֶד אֲדֹנָ֑יו וְאִם־ אָ֣ב אָ֣נִי אַיֵּ֣ה כְבוֹדִ֡י וְאִם־ אֲדוֹנִ֣ים אָנִי֩ אַיֵּ֨ה מוֹרָאִ֜י אָמַ֣ר׀ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת לָכֶם֙ הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ בּוֹזֵ֣י שְׁמִ֔י וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם בַּמֶּ֥ה בָזִ֖ינוּ אֶת־ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: By presenting defiled food on My altar. But you ask, ‘How have we defiled You ?’ By saying that the table of the LORD is contemptible.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the priests of Israel.
The priests present defiled food on God's altar.
God says, "You bring unclean offerings to Me."
The priests ask, "How have we defiled You?"
God answers, "You say, 'The table of the LORD is contemptible.'"
The priests show disrespect for God's altar.
They treat God's table as worthless.
passages.original: מַגִּישִׁ֤ים עַֽל־ מִזְבְּחִי֙ לֶ֣חֶם מְגֹאָ֔ל וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם בַּמֶּ֣ה גֵֽאַלְנ֑וּךָ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֕ם שֻׁלְחַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה נִבְזֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃

passages.text: When you offer blind animals for sacrifice, is it not wrong? And when you present the lame and sick ones, is it not wrong? Try offering them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you or show you favor?” asks the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to the priests.
He says, "You offer blind animals as sacrifices.
This is wrong.
You also bring lame and sick animals as offerings.
This is also wrong.
Take these animals to your governor.
Would your governor accept them?
Would he be pleased with you?
Would he show you favor?
The LORD of Hosts asks these questions."
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ תַגִּשׁ֨וּן עִוֵּ֤ר לִזְבֹּ֙חַ֙ אֵ֣ין רָ֔ע וְכִ֥י תַגִּ֛ישׁוּ פִּסֵּ֥חַ וְחֹלֶ֖ה אֵ֣ין רָ֑ע הַקְרִיבֵ֨הוּ נָ֜א לְפֶחָתֶ֗ךָ הֲיִּרְצְךָ֙ א֚וֹ הֲיִשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֔יךָ אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “But ask now for God’s favor. Will He be gracious? Since this has come from your hands, will He show you favor?” asks the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He says, “Now ask God to show you favor.
Will God be gracious to you?
You have brought these offerings with your own hands.
Will God accept you because of this?”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֛ה חַלּוּ־ נָ֥א פְנֵי־ אֵ֖ל וִֽיחָנֵ֑נוּ מִיֶּדְכֶם֙ הָ֣יְתָה זֹּ֔את הֲיִשָּׂ֤א מִכֶּם֙ פָּנִ֔ים אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “Oh, that one of you would shut the temple doors, so that you would no longer kindle useless fires on My altar! I take no pleasure in you,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and I will accept no offering from your hands.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He is the God of Israel.
He commands the people.
He says, "I wish one of you would shut the temple doors."
He does not want anyone to light useless fires on His altar.
He says, "I take no pleasure in you."
He will not accept any offering from your hands.
passages.original: מִ֤י גַם־ בָּכֶם֙ וְיִסְגֹּ֣ר דְּלָתַ֔יִם וְלֹֽא־ תָאִ֥ירוּ מִזְבְּחִ֖י חִנָּ֑ם אֵֽין־ לִ֨י חֵ֜פֶץ בָּכֶ֗ם אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּמִנְחָ֖ה לֹֽא־ אֶרְצֶ֥ה מִיֶּדְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: For My name will be great among the nations, from where the sun rises to where it sets. In every place, incense and pure offerings will be presented in My name, because My name will be great among the nations,” says the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is speaking.
The LORD of Hosts is a great King.
His name is powerful and holy.
His name will be great among the nations.
This greatness will reach from where the sun rises to where it sets.
People in every place will honor His name.
They will burn incense for Him.
They will bring pure offerings to Him.
His name will be great among the nations.
The LORD of Hosts has declared this.
passages.original: כִּ֣י מִמִּזְרַח־ שֶׁ֜מֶשׁ וְעַד־ מְבוֹא֗וֹ גָּד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבְכָל־ מָק֗וֹם מֻקְטָ֥ר מֻגָּ֛שׁ לִשְׁמִ֖י וּמִנְחָ֣ה טְהוֹרָ֑ה כִּֽי־ גָד֤וֹל שְׁמִי֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “But you profane it when you say, ‘The table of the Lord is defiled, and as for its fruit, its food is contemptible.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to the priests of Israel.
You profane the Lord’s table.
You do this by your words.
You say, “The table of the Lord is defiled.”
You say, “Its food is contemptible.”
You show disrespect for what belongs to God.
passages.original: וְאַתֶּ֖ם מְחַלְּלִ֣ים אוֹת֑וֹ בֶּאֱמָרְכֶ֗ם שֻׁלְחַ֤ן אֲדֹנָי֙ מְגֹאָ֣ל ה֔וּא וְנִיב֖וֹ נִבְזֶ֥ה אָכְלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You also say: ‘Oh, what a nuisance!’ And you turn up your nose at it,” says the LORD of Hosts. “You bring offerings that are stolen, lame, or sick! Should I accept these from your hands?” asks the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He says to the priests.
You say, "This is a burden."
You show disrespect.
You turn up your nose at My altar.
You bring stolen animals as offerings.
You bring lame animals as offerings.
You bring sick animals as offerings.
You present these as your sacrifice.
Should I accept these gifts from your hands?
This is what the LORD asks.
passages.original: וַאֲמַרְתֶּם֩ הִנֵּ֨ה מַתְּלָאָ֜ה וְהִפַּחְתֶּ֣ם אוֹת֗וֹ אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וַהֲבֵאתֶ֣ם גָּז֗וּל וְאֶת־ הַפִּסֵּ֙חַ֙ וְאֶת־ הַ֣חוֹלֶ֔ה וַהֲבֵאתֶ֖ם אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֑ה הַאֶרְצֶ֥ה אוֹתָ֛הּ מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “But cursed is the deceiver who has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it, but sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and My name is to be feared among the nations.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He is a great King.
His name is feared among the nations.
A deceiver is cursed.
This deceiver owns a male animal in his flock.
This male animal is acceptable for sacrifice.
The deceiver makes a vow to give this animal to the Lord.
But the deceiver sacrifices a defective animal instead.
The Lord curses such a person.
passages.original: וְאָר֣וּר נוֹכֵ֗ל וְיֵ֤שׁ בְּעֶדְרוֹ֙ זָכָ֔ר וְנֹדֵ֛ר וְזֹבֵ֥חַ מָשְׁחָ֖ת לַֽאדֹנָ֑י כִּי֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ גָּד֜וֹל אָ֗נִי אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּשְׁמִ֖י נוֹרָ֥א בַגּוֹיִֽם׃
